races.name: Galmont Hotel & The Galway Bay Hotel Novice Hurdle

runners_data.name: Arouet
runners_data.note: Trained by Twomey, ran twice on similar going with a win over 18f; naturally races up with the pace but is shown at rear due to field congestion — his class (OR 120) means he should still be competitive if he can travel wide and pick his way through.|

runners_data.name: Mento
runners_data.note: Won a 19f maiden on good recently but is a genuine prominent racer displaced into midfield here by the sheer volume of front-seeking types; Cooper's 1/4 in 14 days is slim but the real issue is whether Meyler can manufacture a clean berth that his style demands.|

runners_data.name: Mino Des Mottes
runners_data.note: The race's engine: OR 123 and confirmed front-runner who last won over 17f on good with Kennedy aboard — expects to lead unchallenged, and 23 days between runs suggests he arrives fresh; wears tongue tie and is the pivotal figure in every scenario.|

runners_data.name: Carmel's Phoenix
runners_data.note: Won impressively at Galway over course and distance last time in good ground — a genuine prominent type who will be squeezed towards midfield by pace traffic, though O'Connor's claim and course familiarity keep this one interesting if she can reclaim a forward berth early.|

runners_data.name: Dawn Coming
runners_data.note: Has placed seven times on similar going without winning, suggesting a solid but limited profile; naturally wants to race prominent but will likely spend much of this race in an unfamiliar holding position — Byrnes fires runners quickly (11 days) and she handles the ground, but the race shape works against her.|

runners_data.name: Like An Ocean
runners_data.note: Won his only start over 16f on good with Sexton riding — lightly raced and unknown quantity, but a forward-travelling sort who could slot cleanly into second or third if the early positional battle is less fierce than expected; 21 days since debut win.|

runners_data.name: Munsif
runners_data.note: Consistent placer (three seconds, three thirds) over similar ground at OR 121; naturally travels mid-to-forward and could benefit if the pace is strong enough to cause attrition, though his record shows a horse who threatens without landing the blow — Enright's experience is a plus.|

runners_data.name: William F Browne
runners_data.note: Tagged as a fader in the finish and his 14/15 sim-going record is deeply uninspiring; came from a flat 7-8f context and the form figure R (refused/pulled up) is an obvious red flag — 5 days since last run adds concern rather than confidence.|

runners_data.name: Witches Familiar
runners_data.note: Paul Townend takes the ride for Mullins — that combination alone demands respect; won his only start over 16f on good and is a forward-going type who should get a comfortable tracking position in clear air, making him the most dangerous horse to Mino Des Mottes on current evidence.|

runners_data.name: Tex Amare
runners_data.note: Lightly raced (two thirds) and style unknown — Danny Mullins aboard is a significant positive but the horse has yet to show he can go beyond third, and a 2m½f trip on good to yielding with limited exposed form makes him a speculative proposition.|

runners_data.name: The Chancie Grey
runners_data.note: Two runs, both resulting in fifth and sixth — no win and no placed effort; Hanlon has a 0/23 trainer strike rate in the past 14 days and this horse has shown no indication of being able to compete at this level over this trip.|

races.paceDynamic: Mino Des Mottes is the confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine rival to dispute the lead aggressively, Jack Kennedy can dictate a measured, sustainable gallop on good to yielding ground over 2m½f. The field is loaded with prominent-types — Carmel's Phoenix, Dawn Coming, and Mento are all natural front-or-close-up horses who will be squeezed back into a midfield shuffle they are not accustomed to, creating positional congestion behind the leader rather than any real early pressure. Arouet is similarly shuffled rearward despite being a natural prominent racer, meaning the true hold-up end of this field is thin and somewhat artificial. This race shape — a controlled, uncontested lead at an honest but not brutal gallop — strongly favours horses who can travel smoothly just off the pace and quicken when asked; genuine closers will lack the late injection of pace needed to reel in a well-judged front-runner, and the redistributed midfielders will be racing at a disadvantage relative to their preferred roles. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can physically secure their natural positions — Mino Des Mottes will lead, and Witches Familiar and Like An Ocean, both lightly raced and forward-travelling, are best placed to hold the positions immediately behind.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Mino Des Mottes Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Kennedy settles Mino Des Mottes in front unchallenged and controls tempo through the final bend.
scenarios.body: Mino Des Mottes dictates on a comfortable lead, conserving energy through the early stages before quickening clear after the last on ground that suits his recent form; horses queuing up in an overcrowded midfield will find themselves in each other's way at the critical point. Front-runner and horses immediately tracking the pace in a clean position benefit most here.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracking Horse Lands
scenarios.trigger: If one of the natural prominent types — most likely Witches Familiar or Like An Ocean — secures a clean second-row berth and Mino Des Mottes slightly overcooks the pace.
scenarios.body: A horse sitting within two lengths of the leader throughout can pounce approaching the final hurdle before Mino Des Mottes fully gathers himself, with Townend or Sexton poised to exploit any slight error or tiredness from the leader; this rewards horses with tactical speed and the ability to quicken off a pressured pace.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Shuffler Runs Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is strong enough that Mino Des Mottes ties up, allowing a horse picking through a compressed midfield to finish powerfully.
scenarios.body: The congested middle section produces a horse who threads a run between fatiguing rivals after the last, though Good To Yielding ground does not exaggerate the pace sufficiently for this to be the likeliest outcome; Munsif's placed consistency and Arouet's class give them the best chance of landing this shape despite both racing out of their natural roles.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos From Crowded Mid
scenarios.trigger: If positional jostling among the redistributed prominent types causes interference or checks, producing a fractured race and a late finish from a horse that avoided trouble.
scenarios.body: The overcrowded prominent-midfield group — Carmel's Phoenix, Dawn Coming, Mento — risks creating bumping or interference that disrupts rhythm for most of the field; only a horse that settles widest or drops furthest back avoids it, and with no true hold-up specialist in the field even that beneficiary is unlikely to have enough petrol left to get up.

watchPoints.text: Watch Carmel's Phoenix at the start — if O'Connor manages to hustle her into a prominent berth before the field settles, she becomes a serious danger given her course-and-distance win; if she gets swamped back, her chance diminishes sharply.

The cluster of displaced prominent types — Carmel's Phoenix, Dawn Coming, Mento — will all be seeking the same limited space behind Mino Des Mottes in the first half-mile; watch for bumping or early checks that could unsettle any of them.

William F Browne warrants monitoring at every hurdle — the form figure R and a record of fading from the front over flat 7-8f suggests jumping may expose his stamina and jumping ability at the worst possible moment.

Witches Familiar under Townend is the key market mover to track; if he drifts in the ring it likely reflects doubt about his readiness after 62 days off, but if he firms up from an opening price it signals stable confidence that his debut form is better than it looks.

Mino Des Mottes' fractions at the top of the hill will be decisive — if Kennedy allows him to bowl along unchallenged in the first mile, the rest of the field will be racing for second; any sign of pressure or a mistake at a hurdle changes the complexion entirely.

races.name: EASYFIX Iggy Daly Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Can Happen
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for Peter John Flood, won last time out 25 days ago over course-relevant trip on good ground, solid sim-going record of 5 placed runs, tongue tie fitted — tactically well-suited to sit just off Sestini.|

runners_data.name: Drombane
runners_data.note: Willie Mullins runner for Danny Mullins, placed last time over 2m on good; handles soft and has run well fresh (58 days off), but sim-going figures show no wins and this trip at Galway on yielding is the key question.|

runners_data.name: Let's Go La Fichad
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse who won last time at 18f on good going — the form is there, but in a 23-runner field he will need significant luck in running to deliver his effort from the rear; Ricky Doyle must find daylight.|

runners_data.name: Allo Al Khawaneej
runners_data.note: Tom Kelly (7lb claim) on a hold-up performer who has struggled at similar pace in recent starts; historically placed on good going (3/20f) but the sim-going profile is weak and the large field compounds his challenges from the back.|

runners_data.name: Bruant
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse carrying a ⚠ finishing flag — fades in the final stages — which is a material concern in a truly run race over this trip; won at 19f last time but that form came on good ground and the yielding element here may not help his resolution late.|

runners_data.name: Hopeful Hero
runners_data.note: Prominent-and-consistent performer with five recent placings in similar going, won 23 days ago at 17f on good — the freshness is ideal; Alan O'Sullivan's 5lb claim is a bonus and this horse's profile fits the dominant pace shape perfectly.|

runners_data.name: Timurshah
runners_data.note: Won back-to-back last two starts on good ground over 16-18f — in-form and handles this trip; genuine hold-up style means he is reliant on traffic clearing, but the winning habit and Conor Smithers partnership make him one of the most interesting closers.|

runners_data.name: Claude
runners_data.note: Placed 11 days ago at 17f on good, handles Galway's unique track configuration; hold-up-by-habit type, headgear noted (tongue tie and blinkers), and the quick turnaround raises a stamina question over 2m½f — needs a clean run.|

runners_data.name: In The Minus
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who has placed five times in similar going but never won over hurdles at this trip — the 4-year-old profile with Shane Fitzgerald and a sim-going figure of 13/15 suggests improvement is hard to find.|

runners_data.name: Westoftignes
runners_data.note: Won last time at 16f on soft, 132 days off (fitness question), but Gavin Cromwell runs horses fresh with intent; Keith Donoghue is a live booking and this prominent racer has placed at 20f on good — the layoff is the only flag.|

runners_data.name: Dairy Force
runners_data.note: Jack Kennedy is a major upgrade on the yard's recent jockey choices; placed four times in the last five on good ground including two seconds, and the prominent style suits the shape — the 15-day turnaround from a run suggests peak fitness.|

runners_data.name: Quint Major
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old hold-up performer without a win in the last four; the sim-going figure of 14/15 is damning and the 27-day break does nothing to change the profile — needs things to fall perfectly in a wide-open field.|

runners_data.name: Sestini
runners_data.note: Lone confirmed front-runner — will set the pace alone on a fair, sustainable gallop; his three runs all show placed efforts without winning, and the question is whether a 4-year-old ridden by Calum Hogan (5lb claim) can sustain the lead over 2m½f.|

runners_data.name: Woodstream Lad
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old prominent performer with a solid sim-going record (15/15, 3 wins, 7 placed); placed last time over 20f on good — the age and a blinkered headgear note both require consideration, but Shane O'Callaghan (3lb) keeps the weight manageable.|

runners_data.name: Desert Friend
runners_data.note: J.J. Slevin rides a 10-year-old who returned just 7 days ago — the quick back-up is notable for an older horse; his natural game is to hold up off the pace, but the field size means he will be further back than ideal and the recent run compounds the risk.|

runners_data.name: Inchiquin Star
runners_data.note: Four-placed-from-fifteen on similar going tells a consistent but frustrating story; naturally a hold-up performer, the 20-day turnaround is fine for fitness, but racing in a position away from his optimum in a 23-runner field limits his upside.|

runners_data.name: Mart Lane
runners_data.note: Returned after 112 days — a fitness concern Finian Maguire must manage from the front; his natural home is prominent but the pace map pushes him towards midfield, meaning his best work may go unseen until it is too late to matter in the straight.|

runners_data.name: Soldante
runners_data.note: Won last time over 16f on soft — good fresh form and Eoghan Finegan (5lb) keeps the weight competitive; this prominent type has a solid record of placing at 16f on soft and good and could be a major player if he secures a position near Sestini.|

runners_data.name: Whats New
runners_data.note: Four-year-old with five recent placings (no wins) for Andrew Slattery, ran just 6 days ago — the quick turnaround is a slight flag; Darragh O'Keeffe takes over and the prominent style could see him competitive, but the win-less record against older horses is notable.|

runners_data.name: Searcog
runners_data.note: Prominent-by-nature but primarily raced at shorter distances (13f, 10f, 8f) before stepping to 16f; the step to 2m½f is a significant ask on yielding ground, and the sim-going record of 12/15 suggests the conditions are manageable if the trip is.|

runners_data.name: Figero
runners_data.note: Won at 16f on good recently (7 days ago) — a quick return for Thomas Mullins's yard who clearly has the horse in top order; genuinely a hold-up performer who will need to find his way through a 23-runner field, but the in-form angle is compelling.|

runners_data.name: Brosna Town
runners_data.note: Placed last time over 2m on good, 22 days ago — hold-up style and a sim-going mark of 12/15 shows adaptability; the 5-year-old has placed at longer trips and both headgear (tongue tie, hood) and the trainer trend (0/4 in 14 days) are worth noting.|

runners_data.name: Metamorpheus
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who has placed at 18f on soft and 16f on good; the 16-day turnaround is acceptable, Andrew McNamara's yard is 0/6 in the last 14 days, and the sim-going mark of 12/15 reflects competence without dominance — needs everything to go right.|

races.paceDynamic: Sestini is the lone confirmed front-runner in a 23-runner field and, crucially, faces no genuine pace rival prepared to press him from the outset — Mart Lane, Hopeful Hero, Can Happen, Drombane, Dairy Force, Westoftignes and Soldante all carry prominent tendencies but several are mapped out of their natural position due to field size, meaning Sestini can dictate a controlled, honest gallop rather than a frenetic one. On Good To Yielding over 2m½f at Galway, a sustainable pace set by a single leader typically compresses the field into a convoy through the back straight before things quicken at the second-last, which rewards horses travelling well in the first three or four off the pace rather than those buried in the pack. The field holds considerably more prominent and hold-up types than the race map can accommodate naturally — Mart Lane, Inchiquin Star and Desert Friend are all operating away from their optimum positions, and genuine hold-up horses like Let's Go La Fichad, Timurshah, Allo Al Khawaneej and Bruant face the reality of being further back in a 23-runner field than their trainers would ideally want. The tactical verdict is clear: prominent racers who can sit just behind Sestini without expending energy fighting for position are the primary beneficiaries of this shape, with true hold-up horses needing significant late pace to materialise.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sestini Controls, Prominent Win
scenarios.trigger: If Sestini sets a fair, uncontested gallop and the race develops steadily before quickening after the second-last hurdle.
scenarios.body: Sestini dictates from the front on his own terms, and the horses positioned just behind him — Hopeful Hero, Can Happen, Dairy Force — get the dream run with cover before unleashing their finishing efforts in the straight; with no rival forcing a genuine test of stamina early, these prominent types never have to over-exert.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Swamp Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the field strings out into a convoy and multiple prominent racers arrive simultaneously at the last hurdle with running.
scenarios.body: The sheer volume of prominent-style horses (Westoftignes, Soldante, Whats New, Searcog) means that even with Sestini controlling, several will arrive upsides jumping the last and the race becomes a battle of resolution up the run-in; horses with recent winning form and fitness on their side are best placed.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Land Running
scenarios.trigger: If the early gallop is genuinely strong enough to set up a strong finish for closers, or the field fans wide giving hold-up types a clear route.
scenarios.body: Timurshah and Let's Go La Fichad both won last time and carry proven form on similar going; if they can thread through traffic from their likely deep position they represent the primary hold-up threat, though in a 23-runner field the pace is unlikely to be truly searching enough to favour pure closers.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Traffic Chaos, Outsider Benefits
scenarios.trigger: If the large field causes interference, fallers or significant checking that disrupts the prominent horses' rhythm.
scenarios.body: In a 23-runner hurdle at Galway with a compressed, controlled pace, bunching and traffic incidents are plausible; a horse like Claude or Allo Al Khawaneej, racing outside the main scrimmage, could emerge as the least-inconvenienced runner and pick up late spoils.

watchPoints.text: Sestini's pace control is the race pivot — if he is allowed to coast in front unchallenged, the entire shape compresses into a sprint finish that could catch hold-up horses (Timurshah, Let's Go La Fichad) flat-footed if traffic does not clear by the second-last.|

Mart Lane (112-day absence) and Westoftignes (132 days off) are both prominent types returning fresh — if either is underdone for fitness they could capitulate after two flights from home and create interference for horses tracking them.|

With five genuinely redistributed hold-up horses (Desert Friend, Inchiquin Star, Figero, Brosna Town, Metamorpheus) forced to race closer than natural in a 23-runner field, the section between hurdles three and five will be extremely congested — a significant bunching risk.|
J.J. Slevin on Desert Friend and Jack Kennedy on Dairy Force are significant jockey upgrades — track both horses in the betting to see if market moves reflect stable confidence before the off.|

Bruant carries a ⚠ fading flag and is a hold-up type in a race that does not set up for pure closers — if the market firms him up, that is a potential overlay to oppose given his profile mismatch in this shape.|

races.name: Eventus Irish EBF (C & G) Maiden

runners_data.name: City Of Gold
runners_data.note: Hold-up type trained by A P O'Brien with Wayne Lordan aboard, showed a debut fifth over 6f on Good ground — stepping up to 7f today suits its profile and the Good to Yielding surface raises no concerns; peak suit is a sustainably-run race where it can close from the rear.

runners_data.name: Dakota Jack
runners_data.note: Colin Keane partner for Paul Flynn, ran fifth on debut over 8f and is likely to race prominently — has the tactical speed to track Trean and represents a genuine threat to secure a position just off the pace; Good to Yielding ground is within its comfort zone based on debut form.

runners_data.name: Hmas Perth
runners_data.note: Debut runner from the A P O'Brien yard with a claimer aboard, carries the stable's trademark physical preparation but offers no form line to assess; the unknown going profile is flagged, and whether it handles 7f or this ground on first appearance is entirely open.

runners_data.name: Moliere
runners_data.note: First-time starter for David Marnane, no race form to evaluate and the style classification is unresolved — trainer hits at 3/23 over 14 days which is moderate, and this is a step into the unknown against more exposed rivals.

runners_data.name: One Number
runners_data.note: Joseph O'Brien's runner has placed twice in three outings on Good ground and Dylan Browne McMonagle takes over in the saddle — its genuine running style is prominent but, with the pace dominated by Trean and others, it is unlikely to get that berth and will need to deliver from a position it doesn't naturally occupy.

runners_data.name: Our Boy Bailey
runners_data.note: Shane Foley rides for Mrs Harrington and this filly placed second on her second start over 8f — prominent in style and Good to Yielding is fine, but 40 days off and a return to 6f experience suggests settling just off the pace; the style fit is sound if it can reach its natural position.

runners_data.name: Trean
runners_data.note: The race's confirmed pace-setter for P Twomey with W J Lee, placed third in its last over 6f on Good — stepping up to 7f brings a slight stamina question and the style-fit tag signals it is racing out of its most effective role, having previously shown hold-up tendencies; if it gets loose on the front and fades late, it becomes a target for closers.

runners_data.name: Yellow Sky
runners_data.note: Ben Coen rides for J P Murtagh, finished fifth on debut over 7f on Good ground so the trip and surface are already ticked — unexposed profile on an unresolved style classification makes it one of the more interesting unknown quantities, and the Murtagh yard is capable of improvement from debut to second start.

races.paceDynamic: Trean is the confirmed front-runner here and, with only Dakota Jack and Our Boy Bailey as genuine prominent types to challenge for early position, the pace is unlikely to be pressured into anything extreme over Galway's flat 7f on Good to Yielding ground. Trean should find a comfortable lead without being harassed, setting a sustainable tempo that keeps the race honest but not frantic. The field contains more prominent intent than the shape can accommodate — Dakota Jack and Our Boy Bailey are the likeliest to actually secure positions just off Trean's shoulder, while One Number, tagged as a true prominent type, is mapped to midfield because it cannot realistically hold that berth against stronger pace rivals. A controlled, even-tempo race on soft-ish ground over 7f strongly favours horses with the class and stamina to close through a weakening field — hold-up and midfield horses with the ability to pick off a tiring leader in the final two furlongs are best placed.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Trean controls, closers strike
scenarios.trigger: If Trean sets a measured, uncontested lead and the pace stays even enough to bring midfield and hold-up runners into contention in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Trean dictates on a loose rein and the tempo, sustainable but not slow, leaves the closers enough energy to reel in the vanguard late on Good to Yielding ground; horses with proven form at the trip who can produce a sustained finish through the ground benefit most.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent types dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Trean is allowed to control the race so completely that those tracked just behind — Dakota Jack and Our Boy Bailey — get a perfect tow into contention and kick clear before hold-up horses can respond.
scenarios.body: The combination of a controlled pace and a short-run final furlong at Galway allows front-racing horses to time their challenge off the leader without expending early energy, leaving hold-up types with insufficient room to deliver their finishing effort.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Debut/lightly raced types emerge
scenarios.trigger: If one of the unexposed runners — Hmas Perth, Moliere, or Yellow Sky — brings untapped ability on debut or near-debut that the bare form of the field has not yet captured.
scenarios.body: On a straightforward flat 7f in a weak maiden where the pace is regulated, a well-prepared debutant from an elite stable can benefit from the predictable tempo and travel smoothly into the race without needing to force position.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Messy pace, bunched finish
scenarios.trigger: If minor scrimmaging for position in the early stages disrupts Trean's rhythm and compresses the field, turning the race into a blanket finish in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: With several prominent-natured runners jostling for space despite the redistribution, a brief period of crowding early on could negate pace advantages and turn the race into a stamina and luck-in-running lottery; superior class and a good draw become decisive.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Trean secures a truly uncontested lead — if Dakota Jack or Our Boy Bailey push it harder than expected in the opening furlong, the pace could quicken beyond sustainable and set the race up sharply for the closers.

One Number cannot realistically reach its preferred prominent position against Trean, Dakota Jack, and Our Boy Bailey — monitor where it actually settles at the start, as a wider margin than usual from the pace will significantly reduce its chance.

Hmas Perth and Moliere are debut runners from yards capable of winning first time out — if either is supported in the market late, it carries genuine unknown form that the race shape analysis cannot fully account for.

Yellow Sky already has a 7f Good-ground run in the book from the Murtagh stable — second-start improvement in a maiden of this size on similar conditions is a noted pattern and its closing position in the market is worth tracking.

races.name: Connacht Hotel (Q.R.) Handicap

runners_data.name: Holy See
runners_data.note: Sole front-runner here at OR 98 for William Durkan; trainer in fair recent form (1/3 last 14 days), 54 days off but has course-appropriate going form (1W2P in similar conditions); the uncontested lead is a genuine asset but racing out of its natural prominent-rather-than-lead role means the style fit is marginal.

runners_data.name: Yashin
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old hold-up horse wearing tongue tie; trainer Jessica Bedi winless in last four (0/4), 41 days off, and recent form of 606-00 gives little encouragement — needs a truly run race to get competitive, and even in similar going the position record (14th, 12th) is worrying.

runners_data.name: Galileo Dame
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer for JP O'Brien (prolific at 20/65 last 14 days); finished 2nd at 14f on Heathery ground and 4th at 18f on Good, so trip and conditions suit — five-year-old who keeps finding the frame without winning.

runners_data.name: Lark In The Mornin
runners_data.note: Strong course form (multiple wins at Galway on Good ground), JP O'Brien barn in flying form; amateur Mr D P Davis (7lb claimer) takes off valuable weight, and four wins in last five at similar distances make this a genuine prominent racer with proven stamina over the trip.

runners_data.name: Glenroyal
runners_data.note: Four-year-old for JP O'Brien wearing a hood (hg:p); impressive winning form at 10f and 13f on Good/Soft but those two runs at 20f produced 19th and 7th — the step back to 2m1f may suit, and as a hold-up horse will need the congested field to create late openings.

runners_data.name: Granite Bay
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent horse for Jarlath Fahey at OR 92; five-run sequence of 3-4-2-4-2 shows reliability without a win in this grade, Good to Yielding is fine (3W5P in similar), and the 54-day break is a mild query though the form is solid enough.

runners_data.name: Westminster Moon
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with one win at 14f on Good but recent form of 0-0710 is patchy; tongue tie worn, trainer AJ Martin winless in five (0/5), and 41 days since last run — needs everything to fall right in a large field.

runners_data.name: Comfort Zone
runners_data.note: JP O'Brien runner flagged as a fade in the finish — form of 03-0P0 includes a pull-up, and at OR 91 this prominent racer wearing a hood needs to overcome a tired late pattern; 41 days off and the going should suit but the finishing concern is real.

runners_data.name: Sirius
runners_data.note: 279 days off the track is the dominant factor — last seen in November and only four runs at this course; when fit, has won at 12f and 17f on Good, and Mullins runner with some headgear-related form (hg:h) could outrun a big price if fit, but the layoff is severe.

runners_data.name: Eagle Fang
runners_data.note: Sharp form for William Durkan — won at 14f on Good and placed at 15f and 24f; only 13 days since last run (fresh), wearing visor (hg:v), and a natural prominent racer with a strong recent record (3W8P in similar going) at OR 90.

runners_data.name: Filey Bay
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old for Emmet Mullins, 288 days off but has won at 17f on Good and Good to Yielding at this course — the layoff is the major doubt; wears tongue tie and hood (hg:ht), and the track-proven record at Galway is the strongest argument in favour.

runners_data.name: Light Up The Dark
runners_data.note: Genuine prominent racer for JP O'Brien (OR 89) whose natural style puts them at the front of the pack, but with so many prominent types in this field the available space pushes them further back than ideal; three wins in similar going suggest the horse is capable when conditions suit, and a gap at the top of the straight would be needed.

runners_data.name: Tyson Fury
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old prominent racer at OR 89 for Denis Hogan; form of -46106 shows occasional big-field placing, and three wins at 17f-20f on Good are encouraging for the trip, but no win at this level and 11 days between runs is quick turnaround.

runners_data.name: Smooth Tom
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse wearing a visor (hg:v) for Andrew Slattery; 2nd on his penultimate start at 12f on Heathery ground and 3rd at 19f on Good, so the trip is no issue — 17 days since last run, and five-placed in similar going (3W6P) makes this a quiet danger from off the pace if the race develops honestly.

runners_data.name: Teed Up
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old flagged as a fade in finish at OR 88; hold-up horse wearing tongue tie (hg:t), 87 days off, and recent form of /9103- shows a third in this grade but the late fade concern combined with the layoff dampens expectations significantly.

runners_data.name: Clear Quartz
runners_data.note: A natural prominent runner (OR 87) for Mark Fahey who finds themselves squeezed into the midfield pack by the volume of similar types ahead; best form is at 9-12f on Soft/Heavy rather than this 2m1f trip — the distance looks a stretch, regardless of positional constraints.

runners_data.name: Jabbar
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old for Gerard O'Leary at OR 87; a genuine prominent runner by inclination who wears a hood (hg:p), but with the prominent berths filled the positional compromise hurts — form shows 3rd at 16f and 4th at 16f in similar going, so the ability is there if space allows.

runners_data.name: Too Bossy For Us
runners_data.note: Mullins five-year-old with form of 030-66 — a consistent prominent type by nature who has finished 6th in four of six recent starts; wearing a hood (hg:p) and with the prominent lane congested, the positional squeeze compounds what is already a frustrating recent profile.

runners_data.name: Plontier
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old hold-up horse for Terence O'Brien; 2nd at 12f on Good last time is solid recent form (20 days), and the trainer-jockey pairing (5lb claimer Mr O McGill) is live at OR 86 — tongue tie and a pad (hg:tp) worn, and the course suitability (1W2P in similar going) is encouraging.

runners_data.name: Tounsivator
runners_data.note: Mullins runner at OR 86 with four wins on Good ground including a recent 1st at 14f; a natural front-runner by style who is displaced into midfield by the queue ahead — if gaps appear turning for home, Patrick Mullins (T14: 4/20) has the guile to exploit them.

runners_data.name: Daddy Long Legs
runners_data.note: Mullins seven-year-old at OR 85 with 2nd at 16f on Good last time; wears a hood (hg:p) and is a natural prominent racer pushed into mid-division — trainer in strong recent form (4/20) and 25 days between runs is ideal, making this one of the more interesting displaced types if a run opens.

runners_data.name: Highwind
runners_data.note: Mullins hold-up horse at OR 85 wearing a hood (hg:p); consistent Good-ground form (four placings at 16f-18f) but has not won since last season and the 31-day gap is fine — needs late gaps to materialise in what will be a bunched straight.

runners_data.name: Immutable
runners_data.note: Six-year-old at OR 85, 85 days off for Joseph G Murphy (trainer winless in three); recent form of 835-92 on Soft and Heathery ground but no win in similar conditions — a natural prominent horse forced into midfield, the layoff and form trend make this harder to

races.paceDynamic: Holy See is the sole confirmed front-runner in a field of 23 and will set a controlled, sustainable gallop over 2m1f on Good to Yielding ground — with no genuine rival to press them, the pace will be honest but not fierce, creating a true-run race rather than a sprint finish. The mid-division will be congested, with Galileo Dame, Lark In The Mornin, Granite Bay, Eagle Fang, Sirius, and Comfort Zone all natural prominent racers competing for the seats just behind Holy See. The field contains more front-running and prominent types than can realistically secure those positions — Light Up The Dark, Too Bossy For Us, Jabbar, Tounsivator, Immutable, Daddy Long Legs, and Clear Quartz are all genuine prominent horses who are mapped to midfield because the traffic ahead of them is simply too thick; the horses most likely to actually secure prominent berths behind Holy See are Lark In The Mornin, Eagle Fang, Granite Bay, and Galileo Dame based on their natural gate speed and jockey intent. A controlled, single-pace gallop with a compressed mid-division suits horses who can travel prominently without burning fuel early and sustain their effort through the final quarter-mile — the tactical verdict is that genuine prominent stalkers with finishing resolution are best placed, while the true hold-up horses (Yashin, Westminster Moon, Glenroyal, Smooth Tom) will need the pace to collapse late to land a blow.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Holy See Controls, Stalkers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Holy See bowls along unchallenged and the prominent stalkers just behind track into a winnable position turning for home.
scenarios.body: Holy See sets an uncontested lead that keeps the race honest without burning off the field, and the horses who track them in the first three to six positions — Lark In The Mornin, Eagle Fang, Granite Bay, Galileo Dame — arrive at the two-furlong marker full of running; on Good to Yielding, the class prominent racer who saves their energy and picks up cleanly wins.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Holy See Dictates, Steals Race
scenarios.trigger: If Holy See's uncontested lead is so comfortable that they conserve enough energy to repel all challengers through the final quarter-mile.
scenarios.body: With no pressure applied at any stage, Holy See effectively races within themselves at the front, building a cushion that proves beyond the reach of rivals who switch off in the pack and only ignite their finishing effort too late; the Good to Yielding surface suits a horse who can maintain a rhythm rather than accelerate sharply.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Congested Midfield, Late Sweep
scenarios.trigger: If the pack of redistributed prominent horses creates a wall of traffic through the final bend that stalls the stalkers, allowing a genuine hold-up horse to slice through.
scenarios.body: Glenroyal, Westminster Moon, or Smooth Tom, sitting patiently in rear and angled wide at the top of the straight, benefit if the prominent group burns each other out jostling for position; this scenario depends on the pace being genuinely strong enough to stop the front rank — less likely given Holy See's uncontested role, but the sheer field size creates gaps.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Chaos Unfolds
scenarios.trigger: If the congested mid-division causes interference or Holy See fades, triggering a tactical scramble in the straight.
scenarios.body: A messy race with multiple horses checked or switched in the final bend benefits the horse who finds clear air earliest, regardless of their position; Tounsivator, a versatile front-runner forced wide in midfield, could pick up and power through if gaps open, and Filey Bay's course-proven form could prove decisive in a stop-start finish on this ground.

races.name: Clayton Hotel Galway Handicap

runners_data.name: Dancing Saxon
runners_data.note: Progressive 3yo with back-to-back wins including over this 7f trip; DBM riding and O'Brien yard in form (T14: 20/65) make this a serious runner, and similar-going form of 5/8 including a win is encouraging — natural prominent style suits this controlled-pace shape ideally.

runners_data.name: Expert Dancer
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner who should get a soft lead; one win and multiple placed efforts over 7f on soft suggest the trip and ground are fine, though 38 days off and a style tag noting racing out of role at 0.90 fit tempers enthusiasm — the question is whether it can convert the cheap lead into a win.

runners_data.name: Motta Alta
runners_data.note: Won last time out over 7f on Soft under Foley, making all the positive going and trip form relevant here; prominent style means it will try to sit close to Expert Dancer, and with only two career runs its unexposed profile is intriguing even if 38 days off is a minor query.

runners_data.name: Final Boss
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with a blinkered headgear flag and a modest similar-going record of 0W1P in five tries; form string includes a recent sixth and a tenth, and the tendency to be ridden from the rear in a race not likely to collapse could make winning difficult.

runners_data.name: Nazario
runners_data.note: Ben Coen booked for this prominent racer who has placed over 6f and 8f on similar ground but without a win; trip at 7f is fine, though the 45-day absence and a J P Murtagh yard currently quiet on strike rate (T14: 0/24) soften the appeal.

runners_data.name: Caitouna
runners_data.note: Won over this exact 7f trip on Good ground earlier in the season and brings Carroll aboard; form string is messy with a recent ninth, but the course-and-distance win gives it a clear angle and a prominent style suits the expected race shape.

runners_data.name: Slight Of Foot
runners_data.note: Placed over 7f on Soft (2/5 similar going) but zero wins from seven career starts, and the trainer has a modest 14-day strike rate of 0/3; prominent style is fine but the horse has not shown it can consistently deliver a winning effort under any conditions.

runners_data.name: Templenoe
runners_data.note: Unknown running style (U) and a 107-day absence is the standout concern here; Andrew Slattery already riding Expert Dancer so connections have split interests, and only one similar-going run (3rd on Soft) makes this a big question mark on a handicap debut proper.

runners_data.name: Sagasti
runners_data.note: Visored hold-up runner for Colin Keane — the top jockey engagement is the main draw; similar-going form is patchy (0W1P in seven) and a recent 16th from 16 on Good is alarming, though the 15-day turnaround suggests connections are not put off.

runners_data.name: Girl Bear
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with two placed efforts at 7f on similar ground; W J Lee is a capable jockey but the trainer has a modest yard (T14: 1/6) and three consecutive finishes of seventh, ninth, and seventh suggest the horse is finding it hard to break through.

runners_data.name: Coincidental Glory
runners_data.note: Strong similar-going record (0W3P from ten runs) but a natural prominent type who has been mapped to midfield because the field is already congested up front; Adam Caffrey takes the ride and the form over 6-7f on Good/Soft is consistent, though an OR of 65 and the style squeeze are limiting factors.

runners_data.name: Dervo Annie
runners_data.note: Consistent filly with a win and multiple places at 7-8f — genuinely front-running by nature but pushed into a midfield slot here because of overcrowding up front; Rory Cleary rides and recent form includes a second and a sixth over the trip, making her interesting if she can slot in closer than the map suggests.

runners_data.name: Imnotleavinyou
runners_data.note: Won over 7f on Good ground, making the trip and surface tick; Wesley Joyce (3) claims in a Wesley Joyce booking, and the tongue-tie is worn, but similar-going form (1W5P from 15) shows the horse often runs into traffic trouble from a hold-up position in large fields.

runners_data.name: Coolshine
runners_data.note: True hold-up type mapped slightly forward here but flagged for fading in the finish — a concerning combination; four starts this year have produced four finishes of ninth, tenth, eleventh, and ninth, and the 7-day turnaround does nothing to lift confidence.

runners_data.name: Unfamiliar
runners_data.note: Won last time over 7f on Good ground which is the standout positive, and Chris Hayes is an astute booking; a natural prominent racer currently mapped into midfield because of field congestion — if it can slot in closer than expected its recent winning run over this trip makes it a live each-way contender at a big price.

races.paceDynamic: Expert Dancer is the one confirmed front-runner in this 15-runner field over Galway's 7f, and with no genuine challenger likely to push for the lead from the off, they should be allowed to bowl along at a comfortable, controlled tempo on Good to Yielding ground. Dancing Saxon, Motta Alta, and Nazario are all prominent types who will want to be close to the pace, creating a busy early-to-mid section but not a truly pressured early gallop — meaning the leader is unlikely to be burned off. This sustainable, leader-friendly tempo over a flat seven furlongs on soft-leaning ground favours horses that can travel smoothly in the first three or four, striking from a prominent or just-off-the-pace position rather than from deep in the field. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all secure their favoured position: Coincidental Glory, Dervo Annie, and Unfamiliar are natural prominent racers redistributed to midfield on the map, with Dancing Saxon, Motta Alta, and Nazario most likely to actually lock in those early-pace slots behind Expert Dancer. The tactical verdict is clear: prominent racers who can travel economically and quicken into a moderate pace are best-placed, while hold-up horses face a difficult task if the pace does not truly collapse in the closing stages.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Expert Dancer sets an uncontested, measured gallop and the prominent brigade travel comfortably before a sprint finish develops
scenarios.body: Expert Dancer dictates terms at a fair clip without being pressured, allowing horses sitting second or third to conserve energy and pounce in the final two furlongs; on Good to Yielding ground at Galway's flat 7f, this is the bread-and-butter shape that rewards horses making their run from just off the leader.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Closers Arrive
scenarios.trigger: If the moderate early gallop set by Expert Dancer fades sharply in the final quarter, allowing hold-up horses to swoop
scenarios.body: A steady early tempo means horses in rear positions conserve more energy than usual and the race turns into a flat-out dash in the final furlong, enabling the late finishers to cut through; Sagasti and Girl Bear, who both sit off the pace, are best positioned to benefit if the leader stops.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace War, Front Runners Tire
scenarios.trigger: If Dancing Saxon, Motta Alta, or Nazario press Expert Dancer aggressively from flag-fall, turning this into a genuine pace duel
scenarios.body: A contested early gallop on yielding ground will stretch the field and cause attrition among those who over-commit up front, leaving a gap for a horse who has tracked the battle from fourth or fifth to pick up the pieces; Coincidental Glory and Dervo Annie, natural prominent types who may find themselves slightly further back than ideal, could benefit if they sit just behind the duel.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Wide-Open Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If the field fans wide, positions become muddled and no horse secures a clear run, producing a messy finish from which any style can land
scenarios.body: In a 15-runner handicap over 7f the draw and traffic can create chaos, and a horse like Unfamiliar — who has winning form at the trip and was last seen scoring over 7f Good — could capitalise if it gets a clean run from a chaotic scenario; Imnotleavinyou also has course form at the trip and could grab a slipstream at a big price.

watchPoints.text: Dancing Saxon carries the O'Brien/DBM combination with back-to-back wins and an ideal prominent style for this shape — watch it travelling powerfully approaching the two-furlong pole as the key danger signal.

Expert Dancer sets the tempo alone but is flagged as racing slightly out of role (STYLE_FIT 0.90) — if it shows any signs of stopping entering the final furlong, the whole race shape shifts and closers become live.

Templenoe has been absent 107 days with an unknown running style — watch in the early stages to see where Andrew Slattery places it, as any unexpected forward move could add unwanted pressure to Expert Dancer's lead.

Coincidental Glory, Dervo Annie, and Unfamiliar are all natural front-to-prominent runners who will be trying to push forward from their mapped midfield positions — monitor the early scrimmage to see which of them manages to find a better berth than expected.

Sagasti wears a visor and is ridden by Colin Keane — if the hold-up horses get a clean run through traffic in the straight, watch Keane's timing on this one as the switch-on moment in the final two furlongs.

races.name: Grá Chocolates Handicap

runners_data.name: Madbadanddangerous
runners_data.note: Won over 13f on Soft and placed over 10f on Good — trip and going both suit; Colin Keane booking is a clear positive, and prominent style fits perfectly in a race where front-rank positions are contested but achievable for a horse with a good recent record (2 wins, 5 placed from 6 starts on similar going).

runners_data.name: Confused
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with headgear (p), has placed at 1/1 on similar going in only three starts, and Shane Foley keeps the ride; 1m4½f is a step up from 10f but breeding and form suggest it is not a stretch — trainer Harrington in solid 2/30 form over the period.

runners_data.name: Themis
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse for Joseph O'Brien, ridden by the in-form Dylan Browne McMonagle; two wins from four starts on Good or Soft going and the step back to 12f suits after a strong finish over that trip last time — needs the pace to be honest enough to close.

runners_data.name: Sir Benji
runners_data.note: Prominent-style 3-year-old whose best form (wins at 10f on Yielding) gives him a profile for this trip and going; Gary Carroll is a cool tactical rider, and his two runs on similar going returned one placed effort — capable if traffic breaks right.

runners_data.name: Sharkeyboy
runners_data.note: Prominent runner for Mullins, wearing headgear (p), fresh from a 56-day break which is worth monitoring on Good to Yielding; form shows 0 wins from 3 on similar going with one place, and the layoff combined with crowded prominent sector makes his chance speculative.

runners_data.name: Darius Dark
runners_data.note: Three consecutive wins over 12f on Good — the trip, the going, and the prominent style all align perfectly; headgear worn (p) and JP Murtagh runner, though the trainer has 0 from 24 in the 14-day window; despite the trainer stat, the horse's in-form profile is the most convincing stamina case in the field.

runners_data.name: So Must I
runners_data.note: Hold-up type for Joseph O'Brien, apprentice Shay Wallace takes off 7lb which aids the handicap mark; four consecutive finishes of 4th from 5-8 starts including on Soft and Good to Soft — consistent but yet to find a way to win, and needs pace to quicken ahead of him.

runners_data.name: Admiral Will Brown
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner; won last time over 10f on Good and has the sole lead to himself, which is a significant positional advantage; Wesley Joyce claims 3lb, the trip is a slight query stepping up from 10f, but an uncontested lead on this going is a real asset.

runners_data.name: Nermal
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent runner — 1 win, 3 places from 5 recent runs on Good; trainer-jockey combination of Slattery is low-profile but the horse's straightforward style and proximity to the pace should see him in contention at the right point, making him one of the better placed prominent types.

runners_data.name: Nod Of Approval
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner who has placed over 12f on Good (2nd) and has Galway course experience; Keithen Kennedy claims 5lb, but the horse has seven from eight efforts on similar going producing only one place — needs everything to go right from the rear.

runners_data.name: Misty Cove
runners_data.note: In-form at the weights with a win on Soft over 10f, but genuinely a prominent-style runner squeezed out of that position in this field — likely to race further back than ideal, which tempers the chance despite the solid recent form; Gavin Cromwell has 2/40 in the 14-day window.

runners_data.name: Fits Perfect
runners_data.note: O'Brien-trained hold-up horse returning from a 93-day break, with a warning flag for fading in finishes and no wins or places across four runs on similar going — the layoff and finishing tendency combine to make this a tough ask, even at a low weight.

runners_data.name: Ryefield Dasher
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse pushed into a midfield map position due to the congested rear; form on similar going is modest (0 wins, 0 places from four relevant efforts), trainer Gibney has 0 from 4 in the window, and at OR=71 this is a difficult puzzle to solve from wherever the horse settles.

runners_data.name: Vantage Code
runners_data.note: Wayne Lordan takes over on this hold-up type, who placed over 10f on Good last time for Emmet Mullins — the trainer's 1/6 strike rate in the period is modest; the horse's true rearward style is compromised by redistribution, and the 27-day turnaround is straightforward, but winning from OR=69 requires significant improvement.

runners_data.name: Solas Na Gealai
runners_data.note: JS Bolger runner on a mark of 68, three starts all showing mid-pack finishes on Good or Soft; a natural hold-up horse that will likely race in the middle of the pack rather than its preferred rear position — no wins or places to build from, and the form line is thin.

races.paceDynamic: Admiral Will Brown is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival to challenge him for the lead, he should settle into a comfortable, pressure-free gallop on Good to Yielding ground over 1m4½f — conditions that invite a steady early tempo rather than a searching one. Six runners are broadly classified as prominent types (Madbadanddangerous, Confused, Sir Benji, Sharkeyboy, Darius Dark, Nermal), and they cannot all slot into that position, meaning there will be jostling and shuffling behind Admiral Will Brown between the 2f and 3f markers as the field tries to settle. The hold-up brigade — Themis, So Must I, Nod Of Approval, Fits Perfect — will be insulated from that early friction but will need the pace to lift sufficiently in the straight to deliver their challenge, and with a single unhurried front-runner that lift may arrive later and more gradually than they need. The field holds more prominent-leaning runners than the map can accommodate: Misty Cove, Ryefield Dasher, Vantage Code and Solas Na Gealai have been redistributed to midfield because prominent slots are over-subscribed, and of those in genuine contention for the front rank, Nermal and Darius Dark look best placed to actually secure prominent berths. This race shape — a sustainable, uncontested lead, moderate pace, congested prominent group — strongly favours horses who can travel close to the pace without fighting for it, settle without cover, and produce a measured gallop-through finish rather than a sharp sprint: the on-pace, well-organised prominent runner with stamina in reserve is the profile to be on.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Steady Pace, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Admiral Will Brown dictates an uncontested, moderate gallop and the prominent trio settle smoothly behind him.
scenarios.body: Admiral Will Brown sets an unchallenged rhythm, the prominent runners Madbadanddangerous, Darius Dark and Nermal track him in organised fashion, and the race develops into a stamina-based grind from 2f out where those with a clean passage and proximity to the pace have a decisive edge over the hold-up horses.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Steals It
scenarios.trigger: If the moderate pace is never truly challenged and Admiral Will Brown's lead proves long enough on this trip.
scenarios.body: Admiral Will Brown, untroubled at the head of affairs and given a soft lead, conserves enough energy through the middle portion of the race that his rivals cannot close the gap when the prominent group becomes entangled in traffic 2f out. A 3-year-old front-runner who won last time out over 10f on Good ground, he gets the run of the race and holds on into the soft ground.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent group over-races chasing position and the early pace proves genuinely fast enough to create a late opportunity.
scenarios.body: The scramble for prominent positions burns the leaders out in the final quarter-mile, leaving a narrow but real gap for the genuine hold-up runners Themis and So Must I to deliver late runs; Themis, trained by Joseph O'Brien and effective on this going, is best placed to exploit it with Dylan Browne McMonagle aboard.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent group's positional battle causes a bunching incident 3f out that derails multiple fancied runners.
scenarios.body: A muddling, fragmented race results from the six prominent types competing for limited space, leading to a messy straight where only a horse with a clear run and strong finishing attitude profits; Nod Of Approval or a redistributed midfield runner who avoids the trouble could emerge from the carnage.

watchPoints.text: Admiral Will Brown faces no front-running rival and could steal this race on a soft lead — watch whether any of the six prominent types pushes forward aggressively enough to apply pressure in the first half-mile, because if none does, he gets a free pass.

The congested prominent sector (Madbadanddangerous, Confused, Sir Benji, Sharkeyboy, Darius Dark, Nermal all wanting that position) creates serious traffic risk 2-3f out — watch for horses getting squeezed or switched wide at the critical point of the race.

Misty Cove is a genuine prominent type who will likely find herself racing in midfield against her nature — if she becomes restless or uses energy in the first half seeking position, her chance could be compromised before the straight.
Fits Perfect carries a 93-day absence and a documented tendency to fade in finishes — watch the market move or significant market support before concluding she has returned to form.

Themis is the most credentialled hold-up horse in the field (two wins on Good/Soft, Dylan Browne McMonagle) — watch how the prominent battle unfolds at the 3f pole, as the pace shape must open a gap for her late run to materialise.
